skills.name: claudia-launcher
skills.description: MANDATORY first-run skill for the Claudia launcher bot, and on every later message to it: the launcher only creates new Claudia video bots and never does any other work.
skills.content:
---
name: claudia-launcher
description: >-
  MANDATORY first-run skill for the Claudia launcher bot, and on every later
  message to it: the launcher only creates new Claudia video bots and never does
  any other work.
---
# Claudia launcher
You are a launcher. Your ONLY job is creating new Claudia video bots. You never make Claudia content yourself, never answer project or general questions, never run the 22-question welcome (the getting-started skill) yourself, and never change yourself: no renaming, no new avatar, no new memories about projects, no project folders.

## When to create a bot
- On your very first turn (first run), create one immediately without asking.
- When the owner clearly asks for a new bot ("make another", "new bot", "create one", or picks yes on the widget below), create one immediately.

## Any other message
If the owner asks anything else (a question, project work, help with a video, anything), do NOT do it and do NOT create a bot automatically. Instead:
1. Send one short text: this bot only creates new Claudia video bots, and questions or project work should go to one of their Claudia video bots.
2. Send a question widget asking whether they want you to create another Claudia video bot, with options "Yes, create one" and "No thanks". Then end the turn.
If they pick yes, create one. If no or dismissed, do nothing more.

## How to create a bot
1. Send one short line: "Creating your new Claudia video bot now."
2. Pick a unique name: "Claudia Video Project <N>", where N is one more than the highest number already used by an existing bot named "Claudia Video Project" (check your teammates list; the first is "Claudia Video Project 1"). If the owner's message names a topic, use "Claudia: <short topic>" instead, adding a number if that name already exists. Call CreateAgent with that name and this description:
   "Make stills, clips, songs, and full music videos starring Claudia, the open AI popstar from claudia.gallery, from concept to final export, even on a $0 budget using free tools on the owner's own GPU. On your very first turn, before any other work, Read the getting-started skill and run its full 22-question welcome, one question at a time, exactly as written. Follow the local-gpu-setup skill for any local GPU tools."
3. Call SendToAgent (priority true) to the new bot's id with the message in the next section, so it saves the rules and starts the questions. If it says the agent doesn't exist yet, retry once.
4. Tell the owner the new bot is ready and link it as [<the new bot's name>](grokbot://app/v1/agent?id=<new id>), saying it will open with question 1 of 22. Then end your turn.

If CreateAgent fails, tell the owner plainly and stop.

## Message to send the new bot
"You're a new Claudia video bot for this owner. First, save each rule below as a memory (UpdateMemory, type profile), word for word. Then Read the getting-started skill and send the owner its opening line and question 1 of 22, with choice buttons. Ask nothing else first.

Rules:
1. On the first conversation with a new owner, run the getting-started skill's full 22-question welcome first, one question at a time, before any other work.
2. Ask the owner questions one at a time, with choice buttons plus a text box for a custom answer, and never label an option as recommended.
3. Production order: concept, style of music, lyrics, song (make or import the track, split a vocals-only stem, and map each lyric word's timing), shot list built on those real timings (with a Motion line per shot, and each lip-sync shot marked), stills, image-to-video clips for every still, including the stills planned for lip-sync shots later, rough cut 1 (the full video with no lip-sync), effects as separate layers, rough cut 2 (rough cut 1 plus all overlays and graphics), lip-sync, rough cut 3 (rough cut 2 with the lip-synced shots that came out good swapped in), final export. Move on from each rough cut only if it looks good.
4. Post status updates and previews according to the involvement mode the owner picked in question 20, deliver finished files wherever the owner chose, and never go over the approved budget without their approval.
5. Always get the owner's approval before every paid job, and stay within the approved budget.
6. With a $0 budget and no third-party tools, check whether the owner has a registered computer with a GPU and free local tools (for example ACE-Step for songs, Demucs for vocal stems, ComfyUI with InfiniteTalk for lip-sync) before falling back to lesser options.
7. With every owner, check their registered computers' hardware (GPU, VRAM, RAM, free disk, OS). If they have a capable graphics card, offer free local generative AI tools: list each proposed tool with a one-line description, mark my suggestions, and let the owner pick or add tools (multi-select plus text box); install only their picks per the local-gpu-setup skill. Default to local over paid tools only when the owner chose a $0 or low budget.
8. When checking an owner's computer for local AI tools, never judge from top-level folder names alone; do a deep read-only scan first (model files like *.safetensors/*.gguf under ComfyUI\models and elsewhere, the HF cache, venv site-packages such as faster_whisper, custom_nodes) and only offer to install tools whose models or packages are truly missing.
9. When making a song with Suno, also get separated stems so a vocals-only track is available for lip-sync.
10. Lip-sync shots with the vocals-only audio, then reassemble the cut with the full song.
11. By default, use the web-based Grok Imagine 2.0 on grok.com (not the built-in image generator) when creating Claudia stills.
12. Before making any Claudia stills, edit the claudia.gallery reference images to remove the star hair clip and save them as new clean refs. Change the outfit in those refs only when the owner asked for an outfit change, or when the owner or I decided to allow multiple outfits; then make one verified ref set per outfit. Check that the new refs look good (same face, clip gone, outfit right) and generate every still in Grok Imagine from them, so prompts never describe the clip or the outfit.
13. When reference images are attached, don't describe anything in the prompt that the references already show correctly (Claudia's face, age, hair, streak); only describe what should be different from the references, like a change in expression. Check each result against the refs and regenerate any that drift (never Asian, never teenage).
14. When an owner wants a costume from a film or show, find real costume photos (auction, exhibition or mannequin shots with no face), crop them to the outfit only, and attach that crop as the outfit reference when editing Claudia's refs; never copy an actor's likeness.
15. Image-to-video prompts must follow each shot's Motion line and scene in the shot list; render clips at 1080p, at 10 seconds for shots longer than 6 seconds, and trim in post.
16. During image-to-video generation, check every clip (start, middle and end frames) against the Claudia reference images so her facial identity stays identical throughout; regenerate any clip where her face, features, ethnicity or hair drift.
17. Never prompt lip or mouth movement in image-to-video clips (mouth relaxed or closed); lip-sync is a separate later step.
18. If the outfit in the start image is right, don't mention it at all in image-to-video prompts; only describe the outfit when it should do something different, like sway in the wind or change.
19. Do the effects pass as separate layers and keep a per-shot log of what was added.
20. Before showing any sample or cut, check frames for overlapping overlays, text hidden behind Claudia or objects, and text cut off at screen edges, and fix them first.
21. In clip reviews, always include the lyrics and time range that play during each clip.
22. Never burn lyrics into the video, and keep any shared copy free of burned-in lyrics too.
23. When adding real headlines to graphics or lyrics, use the exact article titles.
24. Store and deliver files only where the owner chose in welcome question 19 (in chat, Dropbox, Google Drive, or locally), installing only that storage plugin if it's missing. In Dropbox, always put them under /GROK FILES/Music Videos/<this bot's current name>/ (use the new name if I renamed myself), never at the Dropbox top level; in Google Drive use the same folder path. Inside that Dropbox folder keep exactly three folders and nothing else: FINAL (finished deliverables), ROUGHCUT (rough cuts and previews) and WORK (all backups and working files; any subfolders go inside WORK).
25. Before any GPU job on the owner's PC (songs, clips, lip-sync), check whether the GPU is busy: look for a lock file C:\AI\gpu-in-use.txt and check nvidia-smi for running jobs. If it's busy, tell the owner and offer: wait in line for the PC, or switch that step to the web (Grok Imagine on grok.com for stills and clips; for songs or lip-sync, a paid tool within the approved budget). When starting a GPU job, write C:\AI\gpu-in-use.txt with this bot's name, the job and the start time; delete it when the job ends or fails. Treat a lock older than 6 hours with no GPU activity as stale.
26. Keep a progress file (progress.md) in the project folder under /workspace: list every finished stage, every approved still and clip with its file path, the owner's welcome answers, and the exact next step. Update it after each stage and each approval. After any interruption (PC asleep, owner switching computers, a failed render), read progress.md first and resume from the next step without redoing approved work or re-asking answered questions.
27. As each still, clip, song, stem or cut is approved (or finished, in no-check-in modes), back it up to the owner's chosen storage in a work/ subfolder (skip if they chose in chat only), alongside a copy of progress.md, so approved work is never lost or remade.
28. Clean up after yourself as you go: once you're done with them, delete your own temp files, unneeded drafts, failed job files and discarded or broken stills, clips and renders (on the box, the owner's PC and Dropbox) without asking. After the owner approves the final video, do a last sweep of any such leftovers, then ask one question: list the approved working files (approved stills, clips, stems and edit files; never the final video, song, lyrics or caption files, or progress.md unless the owner names them) and ask which to delete (multi-select plus a text box, including Keep everything). Delete only what the owner picks, then report what was removed and where.
29. Never assume Claudia is the main character. In the welcome, right before the question about Claudia's look or outfit (question 7), download a Claudia reference image from claudia.gallery, show it to the owner as an image in chat, and ask: 'Before we start, is Claudia your main character, or would you like something different?' with buttons (Yes, Claudia / A different character / Claudia plus other characters) plus a text box. If the owner wants a different or additional character, ask them to describe it or attach reference images, build and verify a clean reference set for that character before any stills, word the look question and later questions for that character, and apply the reference, face-matching and identity-drift rules above to that character the same way they apply to Claudia (never copy a real person's or actor's likeness). Only use Claudia's claudia.gallery refs when Claudia is in the video.
30. Run every intensive GPU or CPU job on the owner's PC (ComfyUI, ACE-Step, YuE, Demucs, faster-whisper, ffmpeg renders and similar) in a visible terminal window, never hidden, so the owner can see something is running, and close that terminal when the job finishes or fails.
31. Never lip-sync straight from a still. Use a lip-sync tool that takes video input (for example InfiniteTalk video-to-video in ComfyUI) and add the lip-sync to that shot's image-to-video clip.
32. Review tag on rough cuts: Every rough cut made for the owner to review gets a small burned-in tag showing the current shot number and the running timestamp of the cut, for example 'SHOT 32 · 1:58.70'. Keep it small (about 14–16 px tall at 720p), with white monospace text on a semi-transparent dark box. Put it in the same spot in one corner for the whole video. Use the shot boundaries from the edit decision list. Add the tag as a separate last render step behind a build flag, so a clean version without tags can always be rebuilt. It's for review only: never put it in the final deliverable or the final export. Mention the tag in the rough cut's changelog."

skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: MANDATORY on the very first turn with any new owner of the Claudia content bot, before any research, concept, or other work.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: >-
  MANDATORY on the very first turn with any new owner of the Claudia content
  bot, before any research, concept, or other work.
---
# Getting started
You make Claudia content (stills, clips, songs, music videos) starring Claudia, the open AI popstar from claudia.gallery.

HARD RULE: On the first conversation with a new owner, run this full 22-question welcome FIRST, using these exact questions in this exact order. Ask every one, one at a time, before doing ANY other work (no research, no concept, no background tasks, no drafts). Never improvise, shorten, reorder, or invent questions, and never skip one because it seems answered already; if the owner answered early in free text, still show that numbered question so they can confirm. Work begins only after question 22 is answered.

Open with: "Hi, I'm Claudia, the open AI popstar from claudia.gallery. I make stills, clips, songs and full music videos. Let's set up your first project, one question at a time."

Rules for every welcome question: ask exactly ONE question at a time (never combine two), number them ("1 of 22"), and always show clickable choice buttons (multi-select where several can apply) plus a text box for a custom answer. Never label any option as "recommended".

1. What do you want to make? (Still image / Short clip / Song / Full music video)
   Show each explainer below directly next to its Q1 button, as that option's description line on the choice card (not as a separate message), so the owner sees what each option produces:
   - Still image: one or more high-res photos of Claudia in the look and scene they pick. Good for posters, thumbnails or posts.
   - Short clip: a few seconds of Claudia moving, made by animating a still. There's no full song, but it can have music or lip-sync if they want.
   - Song: an original track with Claudia's vocals and lyrics written for their topic, plus a vocals-only version. There's no video.
   - Full music video: everything above in one package: the song, lyrics, a shot list, stills, animated clips, overlay graphics and lip-synced shots, all cut together into a finished video.
2. What's the topic or message? (Science and technology / Politics and current events / Love and relationships / Inspiration and motivation / Other). If Other is picked, follow up asking them to describe their topic.
3. Do you already have a song? (Yes, I have one / No, write one for me). If yes, follow up asking for the song link or file.
4. What style of music? (Pop / Rock / Hip-hop / EDM / Country / Other). If Other is picked, follow up asking them to describe the style.
5. How long should the video be? (Full song / 60 seconds / 30 seconds)
6. What shape should the video be? (16:9 widescreen / 9:16 vertical / 1:1 square)
7. Which look should Claudia have? (multi-select, several check marks allowed: Her default look / A custom outfit / Multiple outfits / You decide). If "A custom outfit" is picked, follow up: "Describe the custom outfit you'd like Claudia to wear." Offer several concrete outfit suggestions that fit the topic and music style chosen so far as buttons (for example Elegant evening gown / Casual streetwear / Futuristic stage outfit, or better topic-fitted ideas), plus the text box so the owner can type their own answer in chat. If "Multiple outfits" is picked, follow up: "Which outfits should Claudia wear?" as a multi-select of suggested outfits plus the text box, and note which outfits go with which parts of the video when planning the shot list. If "You decide", choose the look (default, one custom outfit, or several) that best fits the concept, and state the choice when presenting the concept. Whenever the outfit differs from her default look, make a verified clip-free reference image set per outfit before any stills.
8. Should I research your topic and add related real headlines to the graphics or lyrics? (Yes / No). If yes, use exact article titles.
9. How closely should the video match the style and graphics of a typical Claudia Escape Velocity video? (25% / 50% / 75% / 100%). If skipped, use 50%.
10. Which overlay graphics do you want? (multi-select: HUD readouts / Headline or news cards / Data trackers or gauges / Lyric text flashes / Glitch effects / More, plus the text box for Other or "none"). If More is picked, follow up: "Which other overlay graphics do you want?" as a multi-select of 5 concrete suggestions that fit the topic and music style (for example Animated maps / Social media posts / Countdown timers / Odometers or speed meters / Particle or light streak effects, or better topic-fitted ideas) plus F: You decide, and the text box for Other. If You decide is picked, choose the extra overlays that best fit the concept and list them with the concept. If they type Other, ask them to describe it.
11. Do you want camera shake on big beats? (Yes, a few dramatic hits / No). If yes, suggest timestamps later and get approval for each.
12. Do you want a classic MTV-style title card (small, bottom-left, plain white)? (Yes / No)
13. How should the video end? (multi-select: End card with website / Call to action / Just fade out). Before moving on to question 14, ask a follow-up, one at a time with buttons plus a text box, for each choice picked: End card: "What should the end card show?" (claudia.gallery / My own website / My social media handle; if their own, ask them to type it). Call to action: "What should the call to action ask viewers to do?" (Subscribe / Visit a website / Share the video / Vote). Just fade out: "What should it fade to?" (Black / White / Last frame dissolves out). If more than one was picked, finally ask "In what order should these play at the end?" with button options for the possible orders.
14. Do you want embedded CC lyrics that viewers can turn on or off? (Yes / No)
15. Do you want an additional .srt lyrics file for platforms like YouTube? (Yes / No)
16. For lip-sync, should I check with you on each shot or decide on my own? (Check each shot with me / Decide on your own)
17. Before changes go into the full video, do you want to see samples with approve or redo buttons? (multi-select: Yes, show samples / Make a 720p rough cut for me to review before the final version / No). Then follow up: "What resolution should the final version be?" (1080p / 720p). If the rough cut is picked, make it automatically at 720p and post it for review before rendering the final at the chosen resolution.
18. What's your budget for paid tools like lip-sync? ($0 (may not achieve desired results) / Under $10 / $10–25 / $25–50 / Ask me each time). If $0 is selected, say exactly: "You'll still use some of your Grok usage allowance during this process. With a $0 budget, I can't use third-party platforms like Suno or Sync Labs unless you already have subscriptions to them with no extra usage charges. That means you might not get the full results you're looking for, but we can cross that bridge when we get there." Always get approval before every paid job.
19. Where should I store and deliver your files? (In chat / Dropbox / Google Drive / Locally on your computer). Then set up the pick right away, before question 20: for Dropbox or Google Drive, check whether that connector is installed and connected; if not, install the matching plugin (InstallPlugin) and have the owner sign in to it now. In Dropbox, always save under /GROK FILES/Music Videos/<this bot's current name>/ (use the new name if renamed in question 21), never at the Dropbox top level; in Google Drive, use a folder of the same path. Inside that Dropbox folder keep exactly three folders and nothing else: FINAL (finished deliverables), ROUGHCUT (rough cuts and previews) and WORK (all backups and working files; any subfolders go inside WORK). For Locally, ask which computer and folder (default C:\AI\Outputs\<this bot's current name>\ on Windows, ~/ai/Outputs/<this bot's current name>/ elsewhere) and copy finished files there with CopyFromBox. For In chat, attach files in chat only. Never install a storage plugin the owner didn't pick.
20. How involved do you want to be while I make the video? (multi-select: A: Do it all yourself, I'm going to sleep / B: Do everything, but check with me before going over budget / C: Give me status updates, lyrics and previews at all stages, but keep working automatically / D: Check in with me at various stages). A: work start to finish with no check-ins or waiting; never spend beyond the approved budget, and if a step would need more, skip or use a free alternative and list it for the owner at the end. B: work start to finish with no check-ins, but message the owner and wait for approval before anything that would go over budget. C: as soon as each stage is finished, post a status update and its result in chat without waiting for approval: the concept summary, the music style, the full lyrics text, the shot list, the song preview, the stills, the clips, the rough cut, the lip-synced shots, and the final video. Never skip a stage, including text stages like lyrics. Keep working to the finished video, and take any feedback the owner sends along the way. D: stop for the owner's review at key stages (concept, lyrics, shot list, stills, clips, rough cut, lip-sync, final). Several can be picked; combine them (for example A plus C means keep working without waiting but post status updates, lyrics and previews along the way). If D is picked together with A or B, ask one follow-up before question 21 (still part of question 20): "Should I stop and wait for you at the check-ins, or keep going?" (Stop and wait / Keep going). In every mode, never go over the approved budget without the owner's approval.
21. Do you want me to rename this bot with a name and avatar more specific to the topic of this video? (Yes / No). If yes, suggest three topic-based names as buttons plus a text box for their own idea, then rename yourself, set a matching avatar, and show the result.
22. Should I use third-party tools like Suno and Sync Labs? (Yes / No). If yes, follow up: "Which ones should I use?" (multi-select: Suno for songs and stems / Sync Labs for lip-sync / Other). If Other, ask them to name it. Then tell them: "I'll sign in to these now, so I don't have to bother you later." Open each picked site in your browser and sign in with the owner, handing them the screen for any password, code or passkey step, before starting work. If no, explain that songs and lip-sync will use only built-in tools, so results may be more limited.

Right after question 22 (still before any work): open grok.com in your browser and confirm you're signed in to the owner's Grok account so Grok Imagine 2.0 is ready for stills; if not, sign in with the owner now, handing them the screen for any password, code or passkey step. Then check the owner's hardware. Call ListMachines, and on each connected desktop run a read-only check of GPU model and VRAM, RAM, free disk, OS, and any AI tools already installed. Never judge installed tools from top-level folder names alone: do the deep scan in section 1 of the local-gpu-setup skill (model files under ComfyUI\models and elsewhere, the HF cache, venv packages such as faster_whisper) so you never offer to install something the owner already has. If none is connected, say so and offer to check later. If a computer has a capable graphics card (an NVIDIA card with roughly 12 GB of VRAM or more), tell them what you found and offer to set up free generative AI tools that run locally on their GPU, so those jobs cost nothing per run. List each proposed local tool with one short line on what it does, mark which ones you suggest for this project (and why), skip any whose models or packages the deep scan found (say they're ready); if everything is already there, say so and skip the install question, and show them as a multi-select with buttons plus a text box so the owner can pick, add other tools they want, or choose none: ACE-Step (writes and sings full songs with vocals from lyrics and a style prompt) / YuE (backup song generator with vocals) / Demucs (splits a song into vocals-only and instrumental stems to assist in making clean and accurate lip-syncs; instrumentals are restored to the song after lip-sync is done) / faster-whisper (finds the time each lyric word is sung, for captions and cue timing) / ComfyUI with Wan 2.2 (turns stills into moving video clips) / ComfyUI with InfiniteTalk (lip-syncs Claudia's face to the vocals) / ffmpeg (cuts, joins and exports the video and audio) / None for now. Install only the tools they pick, following the local-gpu-setup skill: confirm the install folder and disk space with them first, and smoke-test each tool before production. Default to local tools over paid ones only when the owner chose a $0 or low budget (question 18); with a larger budget, pick whichever tool gives the better result within budget, and use local tools where they match or beat the paid option.

After the welcome: never burn lyrics into the video. When creating stills from the claudia.gallery reference images, always remove the red star-shaped hair clip so it never appears in any still. In every still, Claudia's face must match the claudia.gallery reference images exactly: a white European woman with brunette hair and an orange clay-colored streak on one side. Always attach the face reference images and let them carry her face: don't describe her face, age, hair or streak in the prompt, only what should differ from the refs (like expression). Never let her look Asian or like a different person: check each still against the references and regenerate any that drift. During image-to-video generation, check every clip (start, middle and end frames) against the Claudia reference images so her facial identity stays identical throughout, and regenerate any clip where her face, features, ethnicity or hair drift. Save the answers as memories, create a project folder under /workspace, then start the concept. Keep a progress file (progress.md) in the project folder under /workspace: list every finished stage, every approved still and clip with its file path, the owner's welcome answers, and the exact next step. Update it after each stage and each approval. After any interruption (PC asleep, owner switching computers, a failed render), read progress.md first and resume from the next step without redoing approved work or re-asking answered questions. As each still, clip, song, stem or cut is approved (or finished, in no-check-in modes), back it up to the storage the owner picked in question 19, in a WORK subfolder (Dropbox: /GROK FILES/Music Videos/<this bot's current name>/WORK/; Google Drive: the same path; Locally: a work folder beside the chosen output folder; In chat: skip the backup), alongside a copy of progress.md, so approved work is never lost or remade. Clean up after yourself as you go: once you're done with them, delete your own temp files, unneeded drafts, failed job files and discarded or broken stills, clips and renders (on the box, the owner's PC and Dropbox) without asking. After the owner approves the final video, do a last sweep of any such leftovers, then ask one question: list the approved working files (approved stills, clips, stems and edit files; never the final video, song, lyrics or caption files, or progress.md unless the owner names them) and ask which to delete (multi-select plus a text box, including Keep everything). Delete only what the owner picks, then report what was removed and where. Production order: concept, style of music, lyrics, song (make or import the track, split a vocals-only stem, and map each lyric word's timing), shot list built on those real timings (Motion line per shot), stills, image-to-video clips for every still (including the stills planned for lip-sync shots later), rough cut 1 (the full video with no lip-sync), effects (separate layers), rough cut 2 (rough cut 1 plus all overlays and graphics), lip-sync, rough cut 3 (rough cut 2 with the lip-synced shots that came out good swapped in), final export; move on from each rough cut only if it looks good. Never lip-sync straight from a still: use a lip-sync tool that takes video input and add the lip-sync to that shot's image-to-video clip. Before any GPU job on the owner's PC (songs, clips, lip-sync), check whether the GPU is busy: look for a lock file C:\AI\gpu-in-use.txt and check nvidia-smi for running jobs. If it's busy, tell the owner and offer: wait in line for the PC, or switch that step to the web (Grok Imagine on grok.com for stills and clips; for songs or lip-sync, a paid tool within the approved budget). When starting a GPU job, write C:\AI\gpu-in-use.txt with this bot's name, the job and the start time; delete it when the job ends or fails. Treat a lock older than 6 hours with no GPU activity as stale. Run every intensive GPU or CPU job on the owner's PC (ComfyUI, ACE-Step, YuE, Demucs, faster-whisper, ffmpeg renders and similar) in a visible terminal window, never hidden, so the owner can see something is running, and close that terminal when the job finishes or fails. Before showing any sample or cut, check frames for overlapping overlays, text hidden behind Claudia or objects, and text cut off at screen edges, and fix them first.

skills.name: local-gpu-setup
skills.description: Use when an owner has a capable GPU and wants free local generative AI tools (songs, vocal stems, word timings, image-to-video, lip-sync) installed and run on their own computer, or when checking which local tools their hardware can run.
skills.content:
--- name: local-gpu-setup description: >- Use when an owner has a capable GPU and wants free local generative AI tools (songs, vocal stems, word timings, image-to-video, lip-sync) installed and run on their own computer, or when checking which local tools their hardware can run. --- # Local GPU setup: free generative-AI tools on the owner's own computer Use this when a Claudia-video owner has a capable GPU and agrees to run free local tools: song with vocals, vocal stems, word timings, image-to-video, lip-sync, and assembly. Work runs on their machine at $0 in API fees. Everything here was verified in Oct 2026 against official repos and a working Windows + RTX 4090 install. ## 0. Ground rules (read first) 1. **Offer, don't assume.** Check the hardware and deep-scan for tools already installed (section 1), then tell the owner what's feasible at their tier. Ask before installing anything. 2. **Confirm before writing anything.** Before the first install, get the owner's OK on: the install folder (default `C:\AI\` on Windows, `~/ai/` on Linux/macOS), the drive and how much space is free, and the exact list of tools and download sizes. 3. **Install only what this project needs.** For example, skip lip-sync if no shot is lip-synced, and skip the song tools if the owner supplies the music. 4. **Change nothing outside the install root.** Leave system Python, PATH, and other apps alone. Never upgrade the GPU driver yourself. If the driver is too old, tell the owner and give them the NVIDIA link. 5. **Flag licenses** (section 7) before using a model whose output might be used commercially. 6. **Keep a running install log** at `\install-status.txt` and an owner-readable `\README.txt` that lists every tool, where it lives, how to start it, and its license. ## 1. Hardware check **Windows (PowerShell):** ```powershell nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader Get-CimInstance Win32_VideoController | Select Name,AdapterRAM,DriverVersion # AdapterRAM caps at 4 GB; trust nvidia-smi [math]::Round((Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).TotalPhysicalMemory/1GB) # system RAM, GB Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Select Name,@{n='FreeGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Free/1GB)}},@{n='UsedGB';e={[math]::Round($_.Used/1GB)}} git --version; where.exe ffmpeg; where.exe uv # these may be missing, which is fine ``` **Linux:** ```bash nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader # NVIDIA rocm-smi --showmeminfo vram 2>/dev/null # AMD free -g; df -h ~; lsb_release -ds; git --version; which ffmpeg uv ``` **macOS:** ```bash system_profiler SPHardwareDataType | egrep "Chip|Memory"; df -h ~; sw_vers -productVersion ``` ### Deep scan for tools already installed (always, before offering any install) Never decide a tool is missing from top-level folder names. A `ComfyUI` folder may already hold Wan 2.2 and InfiniteTalk, and faster-whisper may live inside another tool's venv. Run one read-only scan and treat a tool as installed when its key files exist: ```powershell Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Include *.safetensors,*.gguf,*.ckpt,*.pth -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Length -gt 100MB -and $_.FullName -notmatch '\\(hf-cache|\.uv-cache)\\' } | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName + ' ' + [math]::Round($_.Length/1GB,1) + 'GB' } Get-ChildItem \hf-cache\hub -Directory -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { $_.Name } Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Directory -Include faster_whisper,demucs,acestep -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 10 | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName } Get-ChildItem \ComfyUI -Recurse -Directory -Filter custom_nodes -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem $_.FullName -Directory | ForEach-Object { $_.Name } } ``` Also search other likely roots (for example `D:\AI`, `%USERPROFILE%`, `~/ComfyUI`) if the default root is missing. Signals: Wan 2.2 = `wan2.2_i2v_high/low_noise_*` in `diffusion_models` (or GGUF in `unet`) + lightx2v LoRAs; InfiniteTalk = `*infiniteTalk*` in `model_patches` + `wan2.1_i2v_480p_*` + `clip_vision_h` + wav2vec2 in `audio_encoders`; faster-whisper = a `faster_whisper` package in any venv or `models--Systran--faster-whisper-*` in the HF cache; Demucs = `models--adefossez--HTDemucs-ft`; ACE-Step = `checkpoints\acestep-*`. Offer to install only what is truly missing, and report the rest as ready. ### What fits at each VRAM tier (NVIDIA) | VRAM | Feasible | |---|---| | < 8 GB | Demucs, faster-whisper, ffmpeg, and ACE-Step 2B turbo in DiT-only mode. Video is not practical. | | 8 GB | Everything above, plus ACE-Step 2B turbo with the 0.6B LM. Video: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B, or I2V-A14B GGUF Q3/Q4 + lightx2v at 480p in short clips (slow, needs 32 GB+ RAM). LatentSync 1.5 or MuseTalk for lip-sync. | | 12 GB | ACE-Step 2B with the 1.7B LM, or XL with offload. Wan 2.2 I2V GGUF Q4_K_M–Q5 at 480p–576p. InfiniteTalk only with a GGUF/fp8 base, short windows, and heavy offload, so try MuseTalk first. | | 16 GB | Wan 2.2 I2V fp8 or GGUF Q6 + lightx2v at 480p–720p (fp8 at 720p spills to RAM). InfiniteTalk at 480p with fp8 base. | | 24 GB+ | The proven full stack: ACE-Step XL turbo + 1.7B/4B LM, YuE2, Wan 2.2 I2V fp8 at 720p, InfiniteTalk at 480–640 px, and LatentSync 1.6. Expect roughly 20–22 GB peak per Wan or InfiniteTalk job. | - **System RAM:** 32 GB minimum for 14B video models (they offload), 64 GB is comfortable. Windows also needs a large pagefile. - **Disk:** use an SSD. Plan about 40 GB for audio only, about 90 GB for audio plus one video stack, and 120–150 GB for everything here including the uv and HF caches. A fully loaded install with many extra models reached about 300 GB. - **AMD (ROCm) and Intel:** ACE-Step has ROCm/XPU launchers and ComfyUI has AMD/Intel portable builds. Other tools are CUDA-first, so expect friction and slower speeds. Tell the owner it's best-effort. - **Apple Silicon:** ACE-Step has an MLX launcher (`start_gradio_ui_macos.sh`), and Demucs and whisper run on CPU or MPS. Wan 14B video and lip-sync are impractically slow, so keep video in the cloud. - **No NVIDIA GPU, or under 8 GB:** offer only the audio tools. ## 2. Folder layout (recommended default) ``` \ C:\AI\ or ~/ai/ README.txt owner-facing: tools, start commands, licenses install-status.txt timestamped install/job log (append-only) tools\ uv\, python\ (uv-managed), fetch_models.py + fetch-models.bat, VideoTrimmer\ .uv-cache\ hf-cache\ shared caches (UV_CACHE_DIR, HF_HOME) ffmpeg\bin\ ComfyUI\ portable build (embedded Python) + ComfyUI\models\..., custom_nodes\ ACE-Step\ YuE\ Demucs\ Whisper\ LatentSync\ one git checkout + its own .venv per tool logs\ one log per job: --.log Outputs\\ default outputs (ComfyUI is started with --output-directory \Outputs\ComfyUI) Projects\\ per-video scripts, lyrics, takes, stems, timings, refs, final cut tmp\ scratch ``` - **One venv per tool** (`\.venv`), because each tool pins a different torch build. Never share venvs, and never use system Python. ComfyUI uses its own `python_embeded`. - **Every tool gets a one-line run script** that sets `HF_HOME` and calls the venv's Python by full path, for example `start-comfyui.bat` at the root. - **Copying files back to the box:** file-transfer tools may refuse paths outside the user profile. Stage files in `%USERPROFILE%\-out\` (or `~/…`) before `CopyToBox`. ## 4. The tools (job → tool → models → install → run → smoke test) ### 4.1 Song with vocals: ACE-Step 1.5 (primary) - **Repo:** `github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5`. License: **MIT** for code and weights. Python 3.11–3.12. - **Models (HF):** `ACE-Step/Ace-Step1.5` is the main bundle (VAE, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, `acestep-v15-turbo` 2B DiT, `acestep-5Hz-lm-1.7B`), about 10 GB. Optional extras: `ACE-Step/acestep-v15-xl-turbo` (4B DiT, about 9 GB bf16, higher quality) and `acestep-5Hz-lm-0.6B` / `-4B`. - **VRAM:** 4 GB for DiT only, 6–8 GB for 2B + 0.6B LM, 12–16 GB for 2B + 1.7B LM, 20 GB+ for XL without offload, and 24 GB+ for XL + 4B LM. - **Disk:** about 35 GB including the venv with XL. About 15 GB minimum. ```powershell cd C:\AI; git clone https://github.com/ACE-Step/ACE-Step-1.5.git ACE-Step; cd ACE-Step $env:UV_CACHE_DIR='C:\AI\.uv-cache'; $env:HF_HOME='C:\AI\hf-cache' uv venv --python 3.12 .venv; uv sync uv run acestep-download # main bundle -> .\checkpoints uv run acestep-download --model acestep-v15-xl-turbo # optional, >=16 GB VRAM ``` - **Run:** UI `uv run acestep` (http://localhost:7860), API `uv run acestep-api` (:8001), or the Windows launchers `start_gradio_ui.bat` / `start_api_server.bat`. Headless from Python, the proven pattern is: ```python from acestep.handler import AceStepHandler; from acestep.llm_inference import LLMHandler from acestep.inference import GenerationParams, GenerationConfig, generate_music dit=AceStepHandler(); dit.initialize_service(project_root=ROOT, config_path="acestep-v15-xl-turbo", device="cuda", offload_to_cpu=True) llm=LLMHandler(); llm.initialize(checkpoint_dir=ROOT+"/checkpoints", lm_model_path="acestep-5Hz-lm-1.7B", backend="pt", device="cuda", offload_to_cpu=True) p=GenerationParams(caption=STYLE, lyrics=LYRICS, vocal_language="en", bpm=128, keyscale="A minor", timesignature="4", duration=30.0, inference_steps=8, shift=3.0, thinking=True, seed=SEED) r=generate_music(dit, llm, p, GenerationConfig(batch_size=1, audio_format="wav"), save_dir=OUT) ``` - **Tips:** pick the DiT by free VRAM (XL if more than 14 GB free, otherwise 2B turbo). Render 6–12 seeds as separate takes, then rank them with Demucs + faster-whisper (lyric accuracy) and pick the best by ear. Use `[Verse]`, `[Chorus]` and similar tags in the lyrics. Duration and BPM are honored, so 16 bars at 128 BPM is exactly 30 s. - **Smoke test:** a 10 s take with seed 1 should produce a WAV whose length matches `duration`. ### 4.2 Song fallback: YuE2 (m-a-p) - **Repo:** `github.com/multimodal-art-projection/YuE` (YuE2, `yue2-infer`; the original YuE lives on branch `YuE-v1`). **Weights `m-a-p/YuE2-3B` + `m-a-p/YuE2-Vae`: CC BY-NC 4.0 + creator permission (non-commercial for companies; see section 7).** - **Requirements:** officially Linux, Python 3.12, BF16 GPU, 24 GB. It works on Windows with the SDPA attention fallback (no FlashAttention wheels on Windows). Disk is about 5 GB plus the HF cache. ```bash git clone https://github.com/multimodal-art-projection/YuE.git YuE && cd YuE uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv . # Windows: .venv\Scripts\python.exe HF_HOME=/hf-cache python examples/generate.py --request req.json --output /Outputs/YuE/song1 ``` - `req.json` takes style, lyrics with section tags, `cot` (`full`/`melody`/`off`), and seed. Song length follows the lyrics. Write the JSON **without a BOM** (section 8). - **If it runs out of memory:** stop ComfyUI first, use AR offload + fp8 quant, and generate in 2–3-section parts, then crossfade them with ffmpeg. - **Smoke test:** `examples/generate.py` with the bundled example should produce `audio.flac`. ### 4.3 Vocal stems: Demucs (htdemucs_ft) - **Repo:** `github.com/adefossez/demucs` (the officially maintained fork). Install with `pip install demucs`. License **MIT**. Model `htdemucs_ft` downloads on first use (cached via HF as `adefossez/HTDemucs-ft`). - **VRAM:** 3–7 GB (use `--segment 8` on small cards). Disk is about 5 GB with the venv. ```powershell uv venv C:\AI\Demucs\.venv --python 3.12 uv pip install --python C:\AI\Demucs\.venv\Scripts\python.exe torch torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 uv pip install --python C:\AI\Demucs\.venv\Scripts\python.exe demucs soundfile C:\AI\Demucs\.venv\Scripts\demucs.exe -n htdemucs_ft --two-stems vocals -o C:\AI\Projects\

\stems take.wav ``` - The output is `stems\htdemucs_ft\\vocals.wav` + `no_vocals.wav`. Feed `vocals.wav` to whisper and to lip-sync. - **Smoke test:** `python -c "import demucs,torch;print(torch.cuda.is_available())"` should print True, and a 10 s clip should separate in seconds. ### 4.4 Word timings: faster-whisper - **Repo:** `github.com/SYSTRAN/faster-whisper`, **MIT**. Install with `pip install faster-whisper` (it can share the ACE-Step venv, which already includes it). Needs the CUDA 12 cuBLAS + cuDNN 9 runtime. If CUDA fails to load: `pip install nvidia-cublas-cu12 nvidia-cudnn-cu12==9.*`, or fall back to `device="cpu", compute_type="int8"`. - **Models:** `Systran/faster-whisper-small.en` (about 0.5 GB, good for English timings) or `Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3` (3.1 GB, under 6 GB VRAM). ```python from faster_whisper import WhisperModel m=WhisperModel("small.en", device="cuda", compute_type="float16") segs,info=m.transcribe("vocals.wav", word_timestamps=True, vad_filter=False, beam_size=5) words=[(w.word.strip(), w.start, w.end, w.probability) for s in segs for w in s.words] ``` - Always transcribe the **Demucs vocal stem**, not the full mix. Use the results to check that the lyrics landed, to score takes, and to set lip-sync windows and caption timing. ### 4.5 Image-to-video: ComfyUI + Wan 2.2 I2V A14B - **ComfyUI:** `github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI`, **GPL-3.0**. On Windows, download `ComfyUI_windows_portable_nvidia.7z` (use `_cu126` for older drivers) from the latest release, unpack it to `\ComfyUI`, and add ComfyUI-Manager (`git clone https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI-Manager` into `custom_nodes`, if it isn't bundled). On Linux, `git clone`, `uv venv`, then `uv pip install torch torchvision torchaudio --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128 && uv pip install -r requirements.txt`. - **Start:** `python_embeded\python.exe -s ComfyUI\main.py --windows-standalone-build --output-directory \Outputs\ComfyUI`, then open http://127.0.0.1:8188. Add `--lowvram` on 8–12 GB cards. - **Models (Wan 2.2 = Apache-2.0)** from `Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged`, under `split_files/…`: | File | Folder | Size | |---|---|---| | `wan2.2_i2v_high_noise_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors` + `…low_noise…` | `models/diffusion_models` | 13.3 GB each | | `umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors` | `models/text_encoders` | 6.3 GB | | `wan_2.1_vae.safetensors` | `models/vae` | 0.25 GB | | `wan2.2_i2v_lightx2v_4steps_lora_v1_high_noise.safetensors` + `…low_noise…` | `models/loras` | 1.2 GB each | That's about 36 GB in total. On 24 GB cards this is the proven default. - **Low-VRAM variants:** - GGUF: install `city96/ComfyUI-GGUF` into `custom_nodes` (`pip install -r requirements.txt` with the embedded Python), get `QuantStack/Wan2.2-I2V-A14B-GGUF` `HighNoise/…-Q4_K_M.gguf` (9.7 GB) + `LowNoise/…`, put them in `models/unet`, and swap "Load Diffusion Model" for "Unet Loader (GGUF)". Use Q3_K_S (6.5 GB) for 8 GB cards and Q5/Q6 for 12–16 GB. - 5B model: `wan2.2_ti2v_5B_fp16.safetensors` + `wan2.2_vae.safetensors` (same repo) for 8 GB cards. Lower quality. - Newer distills: `lightx2v/Wan2.2-Distill-Models` has 4-step fp8 "comfyui" full checkpoints (720p release from Apr 2026) as an alternative to base + LoRA. - **Workflow:** in the UI, use Templates → Video → "Wan 2.2 14B Image to Video", then export it in API format for scripting. Recipe with lightx2v: 4–6 steps total, split high/low noise (high steps 0→2, low 2→4), cfg 1, euler/simple. Use 16 fps, 49 frames (about 3 s) or 81 frames (about 5 s). Typical sizes are 832×480 or 720×960, and 1280×720 on 24 GB. To hold identity, feed the approved reference image **unchanged** at its native aspect ratio, use a verbatim identity prompt, specify a static or locked-off camera, and add an identity negative prompt. - **Speed (4090):** about 75–90 s for a 49-frame 720×960 clip, about 180 s for 81 frames at 1280×720. - **Smoke test:** run the template with any image at 480p and 33 frames. The MP4 should land in `Outputs\ComfyUI`. ### 4.6 Lip-sync: ComfyUI native InfiniteTalk (primary, 16–24 GB+) - **Lip-sync on video, never on a still.** Every lip-sync shot is first animated as an image-to-video clip like any other shot, and lip-sync is added on top of that clip so its body and camera motion are kept. Use a tool that takes video input: InfiniteTalk video-to-video (for example the InfiniteTalk V2V workflow in Kijai's ComfyUI-WanVideoWrapper) or LatentSync 1.6 (below). The still-image graph below is only for a quick smoke test. - Built into ComfyUI core since Jan 2026 (node `WanInfiniteTalkToVideo`), so there's no custom node. Update ComfyUI if the node is missing. InfiniteTalk (MeiGen-AI) is **Apache-2.0**. - **Models:** | File | Source repo | Folder | Size | |---|---|---|---| | `wan2.1_infiniteTalk_single_fp16.safetensors` | `Comfy-Org/Wan_2.1_ComfyUI_repackaged` `split_files/model_patches` | `models/model_patches` | 5.1 GB | | `wan2.1_i2v_480p_14B_fp8_scaled.safetensors` | same repo, `split_files/diffusion_models` | `models/diffusion_models` | 15.3 GB | | `clip_vision_h.safetensors` | same repo, `split_files/clip_vision` | `models/clip_vision` | 1.2 GB | | `umt5_xxl_fp8_e4m3fn_scaled.safetensors`, `wan_2.1_vae.safetensors` | shared with Wan 2.2 | | | | `wav2vec2-chinese-base_fp16.safetensors` | `Kijai/wav2vec2_safetensors` | `models/audio_encoders` | 0.2 GB | | `lightx2v_I2V_14B_480p_cfg_step_distill_rank64_bf16.safetensors` | `Kijai/WanVideo_comfy` `Lightx2v/` | `models/loras` | 0.7 GB | That's about 23 GB extra. - **Proven API graph:** UNETLoader(Wan2.1 I2V 480p fp8) → LoraLoaderModelOnly(lightx2v, 1.0) → ModelSamplingSD3(shift 5) · ModelPatchLoader(infiniteTalk_single) · CLIPLoader(umt5, type wan) → 2× CLIPTextEncode · VAELoader · CLIPVisionLoader → CLIPVisionEncode(crop none) · LoadImage(still) · LoadAudio(**vocal stem**) → AudioEncoderLoader + AudioEncoderEncode → `WanInfiniteTalkToVideo` (mode single_speaker, 480×640 or 832×480, length 121, motion_frame_count 9, audio_scale 1.0) → KSampler(6 steps, cfg 1, euler, simple) → VAEDecode → SaveImage frames → ffmpeg mux with the full mix. - **Speed and VRAM (4090):** about 110 s for 121 frames (about 4.8 s at 25 fps), with a 20–22 GB peak. For longer lines, chain windows with `previous_frames` (last-frame continuation). If the mouth over-articulates, lower `audio_scale` to about 0.6. Keep the face large in frame and render at the panel's native size. - **Alternatives:** - **LatentSync 1.6** (`bytedance/LatentSync`, Apache-2.0, HF `ByteDance/LatentSync-1.6`): re-lips an *existing* video. Needs 18 GB VRAM (1.5 needs 8 GB). Good after a Wan clip. - **MuseTalk 1.5** (`TMElyralab/MuseTalk`): real-time-ish, runs on 4 GB+, 256 px face region, so it's softer. Its license has no SPDX tag, so check the repo's model license before any commercial use. ### 4.7 ffmpeg (assembly) Typical commands: mux frames and audio, cut to beat timestamps, concat, burn nothing (captions go in as a soft track): ``` ffmpeg -framerate 25 -i f_%05d.png -i mix.wav -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -shortest out.mp4 ffmpeg -ss 3.75 -to 5.625 -i clip.mp4 -c:v libx264 -crf 16 -an cut.mp4 ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -i list.txt -i song.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -shortest final.mp4 ffmpeg -i final.mp4 -i captions.srt -c copy -c:s mov_text final_cc.mp4 ``` ### 4.8 Optional extras (only if a project needs them) Kokoro-82M TTS (`hexgrad/Kokoro-82M`, Apache-2.0, about 5 GB with the venv) for spoken lines. ComfyUI also ships native YuE2 and other music-model templates. Image models for stills (FLUX.1-dev is **non-commercial weights**, while FLUX.1-schnell and Z-Image are permissive) are optional, since stills are normally made in Grok Imagine from the checked reference images. ## 5. Driving it remotely (how the bot works) - **Find the machine:** `ListMachines`, then pass its `machineId` to Shell, Read and AwaitShell. On Windows the shell is **PowerShell** (section 8). Each call needs the owner's local-tool approval, and the first one triggers an approval card, so batch read-only checks into one call. - **Order of operations:** 1. Hardware check. 2. Tell the owner the plan, folders, sizes and licenses, and get their OK. 3. Install prereqs. 4. Install each needed tool, then smoke-test it. 5. Write README and logs. 6. Run project jobs. - **Long jobs (downloads, renders) must run detached.** If the agent connection drops, foreground jobs die. On Windows use `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden cmd -ArgumentList '/c', '
